node.label: Masao Maruyama
node.date_label: Essays later collected as Studies in the Intellectual History of Tokugawa Japan (1940–1944) · Logic and Mentality of Ultra-Nationalism (1946) · Japanese Thought (1957) · Approach to Intellectual History (1960) · Reading of Outline of Civilization Theory (1986)
node.description: A historian of Japanese political thought whose Tokugawa studies and postwar writings asked how intellectual change and political responsibility become possible. His 1946 analysis of ultranationalism, 1957 account of historical consciousness and 1960 reflection on intellectual history are read here through Nakajima. Nakajima also criticizes the colonial exclusions of his democratic nationalism; Lim questions the deterministic account of China in the Tokugawa studies. The existing comparison with modernization theory remains a comparison of questions, not an affiliation.
node.representative_figures_and_works: Studies in the Intellectual History of Tokugawa Japan (essays 1940–44; Japanese collection 1952; English translation by Mikiso Hane 1974); Logic and Mentality of Ultra-Nationalism (1946); Japanese Thought (original essay 1957; later collected separately); Approach to Intellectual History (1960); Thought and Behaviour in Modern Japanese Politics (English 1963; expanded 1969); Reading of Outline of Civilization Theory (1986).
node.scope_note: Read on 2026-10-24: Nakajima’s selected chapter pages and Lim’s English abstract; NDL catalogue metadata. The original Japanese essays and 1986 commentary remain unread, known through named readers. The prior source’s narrower primary-opening review is retained, including its caution about the platform’s 1989 reissue description. The 1952 collection, 1974 translation and 1940–44 essays are distinct. Existing person ID and intellectual-history roster wording are preserved.
